@mongo__findOne.summary: Find a single document. Runtime kind `FIND_ONE`.

authors.intro: Find a single document. Pair with `@transport(kind: "mongo")`.
authors.example:
user(id: ID!): User
  @mongo__findOne(
    collection: "users"
    query: "_id: $args.id"
    selection: """
id: _id
name
"""
  )

implementers.loaders: Schemas that use `@mongo__*` must `@link` this family and import the directive names used.
implementers.runtime: On resolve: build the Mongo operation for this directive, run it against `collection`, then project the result with `selection`. Store/operation errors become GraphQL field errors.
implementers.validation: Require non-empty `collection` for executable apps. `subgraph`, when present, must match the composition subgraph name. Binder strings must parse; reject unknown args for this directive.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition - the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute the directive to that composition subgraph name. Use the same string as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and other directives for the source. Never invent a second name for the same source.

query.constraints: Filter binder (`$args.filter`, `_id: $args.id`, merge blocks). Client GraphQL often uses `filter` while binders keep Mongo-style `query`.
query.authors: How to build the Mongo filter from args/parent.

selection.authors: Project Mongo fields into GraphQL fields (e.g. `id: _id`). Nested blocks shape connection payloads.
selection.implementers:
When it runs: After the operation returns document(s) (or a mutation payload), before the GraphQL field completes.

Input: Returned document(s) and the `selection` mapping lines (`graphqlField: mongoPath` / `_id`, nested blocks).

Output: GraphQL object(s) with only the selected fields, renamed as mapped (e.g. `id: _id`).

Errors: Missing paths yield null/omit per GraphQL nullability; mapping parse errors fail setup.
